1.0 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To define the policy for appropriate pain management.

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 Hospital Management

2.2 Health Care Providers

2.3 Patients

2.4 Government agencies

3.0 RESPONSIBILITY:

3.1 Doctors

3.2 Nursing staff

4.0 ABBREVIATIONS:

4.1 COP- Care of patients

5.0 DEFINITION:

5.1 Pain is whatever the patient says it is. The pain experience is a mixture of physical sensations, physiologic changes, and psychosocial factors. The patient’s interpretation of the physical sensation is influenced by the patient’s culture, previous experience with and without pain, beliefs about self, interpretation of the future, present environment, and the persons in that environment.

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH :Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1. Documented policies and procedures guide the management of pain.

7.2. Patients with pain undergo detailed assessment and periodic re-assessment.

7.3. The organization respects and supports the management of pain for all patients.

7.4. Patient and family are educated on various pain management techniques, where appropriate.

8. 0 PROCESSES

The purpose of this policy is to define proper assessment of pain including pain scales, initial and ongoing assessment and proper documentation in the electronic medical record

8.1 Pain scales shall be used to determine the intensity and level of pain. Visual Analog Scale (Happy/Sad faces) shall be selected

8.1.1 Pain Assessment shall be completed upon admission, during routine physical assessments and when the patient experiences a pain event. - On admission, complete the pain review. - Pain assessment shall include: pain location and site, description and intensity. A pain management plan of care shall be established based on the patient’s clinical presentation, individualized comfort.

8.1.2 Ayurveda Approach to Pain Management

• Pain management in Ayurveda would start with identifying and correcting the dosha imbalance. Specific measures would be recommended to find relief from pain as well as counseling would generally be provided to enhance the positive attitude and forbearance.

• Proper detoxification is considered mandatory to undo the underlying cause interfering with stimulation of nerves resulting into pain sensation.

Enhancing the Agni is considered essential. This is brought about by Ayurvedic medications & Ayurveda therapies for boosting digestion. It includes number of herbs like Garlic, Ginger, Guggulu, Turmeric, Shilajit

• Rasna, Nirgundi, Ashwagandha (Withaniasomnifera), Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus ) , Eranda (Ricinus Communis) , Sallaki ( Boswellia serrata) , Guggulu (Commiphora mukul) etc are generally recommended for relieving the pain.

• Along with this, Ayurveda counsels proper stretching and flexibility exercises to ease the circulation and functions of the nervous system. Yoga asanas and Pranayama (Deep Breathing techniques), Physiotherapy are beneficial add-on therapies included in pain management.

8.1.3 Pain management by some therapies –

1. Snehan & Swedan: The procedure includes application of medicated oil which is selected according to type of pain followed by sudation therapy (steam, dry heat, patrapottali, pindasweda, etc.) Usually done in cases of sprain, back ache, muscular injury as in sports injury. Kati Basti, Janu Basti, Manya Basti, Hrid Basti are organ related procedures performed at respective site to manage pain and to strengthen them.In some cases of abdominal pain like renal colic or accumulation of gases Basti treatment is selected.

2. Agnikarma : It works effectively and gives immediate relief in conditions like joint pain, pain due to cervical or lumbar spondylosis and sciatica

3. Blood letting : Blood letting again is performed in various ways the common methods used in practice are : -

a) Jalaukavcharan (Leech therapy) – It is indicated in headache, some skin diseases, swelling in various tissues or joints, pain due to contused wound where blood capillaries get ruptured and the blood gets accumulated under the skin resulting in pain.

b) Blood letting by syringe or scalp vein wherein blood is removed by puncturing the vein.

4. Lepa : It is the application of paste of herbs on the affected area and leave it to dry. Usually applied in cases of swelling, injury, sprain, etc.

All these procedures should be carried out under guidance of an Ayurvedic consultant only.

8.1.4 Pain Medication Side Effects and Pain Relief Reassessment

1. Medication side effects shall be assessed.

2. Pain relief may include pain intensity; patient statement of adequate relief; or absence/ decrease of nonverbal pain indicators in the non-communicative patient.

8.1.5 Documentation in the Medical Record shall include:

1. Admission pain review

2. Pain screening during routine physical assessment

3. Pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic pain intervention

4. Medication side effects

5. Evidence of pain relief

6. Patient education

7. If not relieved patient is refer to SMHRC for further management

8.1.6: Patient and family are educated on various pain management techniques it could be done only for patients who are likely to have long term pain or in view of the underlying condition not being treatable.
